findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When the Integration row does not exist yet (install redirect beats the webhook), DoesNotExist calls next_step and skips the sender check, so an attacker who has the installation_id can race the webhook and bind the victim's installation to their own org.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]` raises KeyError (500) for Integrations built through the pipeline, because build_integration only sets sender when state has it. This affects every legacy or orphaned integration being reinstalled.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which is deterministic and not a per-session nonce (the tests hardcode 9cae5e88...), so an attacker can forge the callback or CSRF a victim into completing it with the attacker's code.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:501 — The check compares the mutable GitHub `login` and requires the Sentry-side user to be the same person who clicked install. Org installs where another admin (or a renamed account) installed the app are falsely rejected. It should compare the immutable user id or check org admin membership instead.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:449 — GitHubInstallation still prefers request.GET installation_id over the id bound during OAuth, so a later request can swap in a different installation_id after authentication. The check only holds if that id's sender happens to match.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." text, which every failure path returns (bad state, token failure, DoesNotExist), so it would still pass if the sender comparison were broken.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info and safe_urlopen failures (network errors or a GitHub error response) are not caught and cause a 500, and a GitHub `error=access_denied` callback gets no dedicated handling.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — A non-ACTIVE existing Integration (e.g. disabled) with no OrganizationIntegration used to reinstall via next_step but now hits a hard error. This is a behavior regression.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The authorize redirect URL is built with an f-string without URL-encoding redirect_uri or state.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (500) for existing integrations created without a sender, since build_integration only sets sender conditionally (line 376).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:425 — safe_urlopen sits outside the try block, and get_user_info (line 435) isn't guarded either, so network or identity errors propagate as 500s instead of the error() page.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The second lookup adds status=ACTIVE, so an existing non-active Integration that has no OrganizationIntegration now hits the generic error page where it used to proceed to next_step.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:398 — OAuthLoginView binds installation_id from request.GET before the state/signature check, so an unauthenticated callback can overwrite pipeline state before validation.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — The Integration.DoesNotExist path returns next_step without comparing sender, so the new identity check only covers integrations already in the DB and a webhook race decides whether the check runs.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView re-implements OAuth2 token exchange ("similar to OAuth2CallbackView...") instead of reusing/subclassing OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView, duplicating logic that will drift.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — Module-level function named generic `error` is ambiguous and easily shadowed (e.g. by local `error` vars/exception names); name it e.g. render_installation_error.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` applies gettext to a runtime variable, so literal call-site strings are never extracted for translation; mark literals with _() at call sites instead.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — New `error()` helper lacks type hints for request/org/error_short/error_long and return type, weakening the type boundary in a mypy-checked module.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:149 — get_document_origin(org) has an untyped `org` parameter (RpcUserOrganizationContext | None).
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch leaves `pipeline` untyped unlike sibling GitHubInstallation.dispatch (pipeline: Pipeline).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:19 — Integration module now imports identity-provider internals (GitHubIdentityProvider, get_user_info) and hand-calls its URL/secret getters, coupling integration and identity layers.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — Bare `except Exception` silently swallows token-response decode errors with no logging, hiding OAuth failures from diagnosis.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize URL built via f-string concatenation without urlencode for redirect_uri/state; use urlencode for correctness and readability.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:397 — installation_id binding is split across OAuthLoginView and GitHubInstallation (bound in both), making state ownership unclear.
src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:41 — Removed FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR constant in favor of hardcoded "github" literal; unrelated refactor to intent that reduces extensibility.
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Magic pipeline-signature string and code/state setup URL are duplicated across many tests; extract a helper/constant.
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Test asserts on responses.calls[2] positional index, brittle coupling to stub call ordering.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen token exchange is outside the try block, so network errors/timeouts/RestrictedIPAddress propagate as an unhandled 500 instead of the error page.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is uncaught and raises (raise_for_status/JSON decode) on GitHub 401/5xx/rate limit, crashing the pipeline with a 500.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Token exchange response status is never checked; non-200 GitHub responses are only detected indirectly via a missing access_token with no reason surfaced.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:429 — Broad except Exception swallows read/decode failures with no logging or metrics, making OAuth failures undiagnosable.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:438 — All OAuth failure branches (state mismatch, no access_token, no login, GitHub error payload) return a generic error with no logger/metrics call.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for existing integrations whose metadata lacks sender, causing a 500 for reinstalls.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Synchronous OAuth token exchange and user lookup run in the request thread with no retry and only the default safe_urlopen timeout, so a slow GitHub can hang the web worker.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — If the GitHub /user payload is not a dict (e.g. an error list or None), the `"login" in` check can raise TypeError instead of returning the error page.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook not received), GitHubInstallation calls next_step without any sender/authenticated-user check, so an attacker can claim a victim's fresh installation_id and bypass the new verification.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:447 — installation_id taken from request.GET on the post-OAuth request overrides the value bound before authorization, letting the ID be swapped after the OAuth step; only the Integration-exists branch re-validates it.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize redirect URL built with f-string without URL-encoding client_id/state/redirect_uri (redirect_uri contains ://, /), risking malformed or parameter-injected OAuth requests; use urlencode.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuth state compared to pipeline.signature with != (non-constant-time) and state is a static per-pipeline signature rather than a fresh random nonce; use constant_time_compare.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:398 — installation_id from the initial GET is bound into pipeline state before OAuth with no validation, and the check at 503 assumes integration.metadata["sender"] exists (KeyError -> 500 instead of a safe denial).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — Broad except Exception around the token exchange silently swallows errors and GitHub error responses (e.g. bad_verification_code) with no logging, hindering detection of abuse.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:388 — test_installation_not_found now fails at the OAuth state check (different hardcoded state), so it no longer exercises the "installation could not be found" path it was written to test.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — The only negative assertion is the generic "Invalid installation request." string, which the state-mismatch, missing-token, missing-login, inactive-integration, and sender-mismatch branches all return, so the test can't tell which guard fired.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Hardcoded pipeline.signature values ("9cae5e88..."/"ddd023d8...") tie the tests to how signatures are generated and to fixture ordering, so they break for reasons unrelated to OAuth behavior.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — No dedicated test sends a forged/mismatched state and asserts the error, so the core CSRF guard is only covered by accident.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:431 — No test covers a token-exchange response missing access_token (e.g. GitHub error=bad_verification_code) or an unparseable body.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — No test covers get_user_info failing (non-200 /user), which likely raises out of dispatch as a 500 instead of rendering the error page.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:435 — No test covers a /user response that lacks "login".

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — Only the mismatch case is tested; no test shows an existing Integration without an OrganizationIntegration succeeding when the sender login matches the authenticated user, nor covers missing metadata["sender"] (KeyError).
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:495 — The new branch for an existing Integration that is not ACTIVE is untested.
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — responses.calls[2] is a brittle positional index that depends on the number and order of the OAuth HTTP calls.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:123 — The mocked token and /user responses are never asserted on (code/client_secret in the POST body, token in the Authorization header), so the tests would pass even if the wrong code or token were sent.

src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:41 — The FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR removal and the new OAuth redirect_uri to the setup URL have no pipeline_advancer test (e.g. an OAuth callback with state but no pipeline).

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:229 — No test covers a direct-from-GitHub install where installation_id arrives on the OAuth view and must survive through pipeline state into GitHubInstallation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When the Integration row does not exist yet (install redirect beats the webhook), DoesNotExist calls next_step and skips the sender check, so an attacker who has the installation_id can race the webhook and bind the victim's installation to their own org.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code still has an early `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` when looking up `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` (now using `installation_id` from GET/state). The new authenticity check (comparing `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) only runs later in the branch where an `Integration` *does* exist. Therefore, if the `Integration` row does not exist yet, the request proceeds to the next pipeline step without any sender/authenticated-user validation, matching the finding’s bypass description.

This affects every legacy or orphaned integration being reinstalled.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which is deterministic and not a per-session nonce (the tests hardcode 9cae5e88...), so an attacker can forge the callback or CSRF a victim into completing it with the attacker's code.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the OAuth state parameter is set to pipeline.signature, which is deterministic/static rather than a per-request/session random nonce, enabling CSRF/forged callback. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:501 — The check compares the mutable GitHub `login` and requires the Sentry-side user to be the same person who clicked install. Org installs where another admin (or a renamed account) installed the app are falsely rejected. It should compare the immutable user id or check org admin membership instead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new validation in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` that rejects when `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` (i.e., compares GitHub usernames/logins). This indeed enforces that the GitHub account completing the OAuth step must match the GitHub `sender` who installed the app, and it relies on the mutable `login` string rather than an immutable identifier. However, the PR also adds an explicit test (`test_github_user_mismatch`) asserting this rejection behavior, indicating it is intentional (a security/anti-hijack measure) rather than an accidental defect. The review concern is still real and diff-grounded as a product/UX/robustness issue (renames / other admins), but it’s not a verifiable “bug” given the intended behavior in tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:449 — GitHubInstallation still prefers request.GET installation_id over the id bound during OAuth, so a later request can swap in a different installation_id after authentication. The check only holds if that id's sender happens to match.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is resolved as `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`, which explicitly prioritizes a querystring `installation_id` over the one previously bound into pipeline state during the OAuth step. The code then immediately `bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`, so a subsequent request can replace the previously authenticated/bound installation id. The later authenticated-user vs installer check only runs in the branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` already exists (`integration = Integration.objects.get(...);` then compare `github_authenticated_user` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`); if `Integration.DoesNotExist`, it proceeds to `pipeline.next_step()` without any equivalent validation, so a swapped `installation_id` can advance the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch only asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." text, which every failure path returns (bad state, token failure, DoesNotExist), so it would still pass if the sender comparison were broken.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, all of these failure paths return the same generic `error_short` text via `error()` (defaulting to "Invalid installation request."): OAuth state mismatch (`OAuthLoginView`), token parsing/access_token missing, missing `login` from `get_user_info`, `Integration.DoesNotExist` in `GitHubInstallation`, and the new sender/login mismatch check. The new test `test_github_user_mismatch` only asserts that generic text is present (and that the failure template is used), so it does not uniquely validate that the failure was caused by the sender/login comparison (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage weakness rather than a product bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info and safe_urlopen failures (network errors or a GitHub error response) are not caught and cause a 500, and a GitHub `error=access_denied` callback gets no dedicated handling.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the call to `safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` is not wrapped in a try/except, and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also not protected. Network errors or HTTP-level failures from GitHub during token exchange/user lookup can therefore raise and bubble up as a 500. Additionally, the OAuth callback path only checks `state` and then blindly attempts token exchange using `code = request.GET.get("code")`; a GitHub callback like `?error=access_denied&state=...` (no `code`) gets no dedicated handling and will proceed into token exchange rather than returning a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — A non-ACTIVE existing Integration (e.g. disabled) with no OrganizationIntegration used to reinstall via next_step but now hits a hard error. This is a behavior regression.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the prior behavior for the case “Integration exists but no OrganizationIntegration exists” was to `pipeline.next_step()` unconditionally after binding `installation_id`. The diff changes this to `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and returns `error(...)` on `Integration.DoesNotExist`. That means an existing non-ACTIVE integration (e.g. disabled) now fails the flow instead of proceeding to re-link/reinstall, which is a clear behavior change/regression grounded in the added status filter and hard error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The authorize redirect URL is built with an f-string without URL-encoding redirect_uri or state.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the authorize URL is manually assembled via an f-string: `...&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` without using `urlencode`/quoting. That is verifiable from the diff. However, both `state` (pipeline signature) and `redirect_uri` (server-generated `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`) are not user-controlled here, and the added tests explicitly expect the unencoded `redirect_uri=http://testserver/...` in the query string, so it’s not clearly a broken behavior/security defect as shown—more a robustness/correctness improvement for proper query construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (500) for existing integrations created without a sender, since build_integration only sets sender conditionally (line 376).
matched_golden_ids: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the code directly indexes into integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without ensuring the "sender" key exists, leading to a KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata (since sender is set conditionally during creation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:425 — safe_urlopen sits outside the try block, and get_user_info (line 435) isn't guarded either, so network or identity errors propagate as 500s instead of the error() page.

adjudication.rationale: In the new OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the network call `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is executed outside the `try` block, and only `safe_urlread(req)`/parsing is guarded. If `safe_urlopen` raises (e.g., network/timeout/HTTP issues), it will propagate and likely 500 instead of returning `error(...)`. Similarly, `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is unguarded; if that function performs a network request or raises on invalid responses, it will also bubble up as a 500 rather than the intended error page. This behavior is directly visible in the diff and contradicts the error-handling pattern used elsewhere in the flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The second lookup adds status=ACTIVE, so an existing non-active Integration that has no OrganizationIntegration now hits the generic error page where it used to proceed to next_step.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the behavior described: in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code now does `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and returns `error(...)` on `DoesNotExist`, whereas previously this path simply bound `installation_id` and proceeded to `pipeline.next_step()` even if the existing `Integration` was non-active. However, whether treating a non-ACTIVE, unlinked `Integration` as an error is a defect cannot be determined from the diff alone—it may be an intentional tightening to only accept verified/active installations before doing the authenticated-user check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:398 — OAuthLoginView binds installation_id from request.GET before the state/signature check, so an unauthenticated callback can overwrite pipeline state before validation.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the code reads `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id")` and immediately calls `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)` before any validation of the OAuth callback `state` (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`). This means a request (including one with an invalid/missing `state`) can mutate pipeline state prior to authenticity checks, enabling pipeline-state poisoning/overwriting via an unauthenticated/invalid callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — The Integration.DoesNotExist path returns next_step without comparing sender, so the new identity check only covers integrations already in the DB and a webhook race decides whether the check runs.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code only performs the new identity check (`pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') != integration.metadata['sender']['login']`) after successfully loading an existing `Integration` (the later `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)`). If the earlier lookup used inside the `OrganizationIntegration.objects.filter(integration=Integration.objects.get(...))` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the handler immediately does `return pipeline.next_step()` without any sender/login comparison. That makes the new protection apply only when an `Integration` already exists in the DB; whether an `Integration` exists at that moment can depend on timing (e.g., webhook-created integration vs. not yet created). The diff doesn’t prove this is exploitable or broken end-to-end (it depends on what later pipeline steps do), but it is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in the intended check coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView re-implements OAuth2 token exchange ("similar to OAuth2CallbackView...") instead of reusing/subclassing OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView, duplicating logic that will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OAuthLoginView` that manually performs the OAuth authorize redirect and token exchange: it builds `data` with `code/client_id/client_secret`, calls `safe_urlopen` to `ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url()`, reads/parses the response via `safe_urlread(...).decode(...)` and `dict(parse_qsl(body))`, and contains comments explicitly stating it's “similar to OAuth2CallbackView...”. This is duplicated OAuth2 callback logic rather than reusing existing OAuth2 view classes, creating a concrete maintainability/architecture risk (logic drift) introduced by this change, but it’s not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — Module-level function named generic `error` is ambiguous and easily shadowed (e.g. by local `error` vars/exception names); name it e.g. render_installation_error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a module-level helper named `error(...)` (around integration.py:126), but the finding is purely a naming/style preference. The diff shows no actual shadowing, misuse, or behavioral defect caused by the name `error`, and Python scope rules make accidental shadowing a hypothetical concern rather than a diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` applies gettext to a runtime variable, so literal call-site strings are never extracted for translation; mark literals with _() at call sites instead.

adjudication.rationale: The new `error()` helper wraps `error_short` with `_()` at render time (`"data": {"error": _(error_short)}`), but call sites pass plain string literals (e.g. `error_short="Github installed on another Sentry organization."`, `"GitHub installation pending deletion."`) without `_()`. Django message extraction typically only collects strings passed to gettext at the call site, so these literals likely won’t be extracted into translation catalogs and therefore won’t be translated in non-English locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — New `error()` helper lacks type hints for request/org/error_short/error_long and return type, weakening the type boundary in a mypy-checked module.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new helper `def error(request, org, error_short=..., error_long=...):` (around integration.py:129) with no type annotations on parameters or return type. Given the surrounding file uses `typing` imports and typed signatures elsewhere (e.g., `get_document_origin(org) -> str`, `dispatch(self, request: Request, pipeline) -> HttpResponse`), this is a concrete, diff-grounded type-coverage regression rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:149 — get_document_origin(org) has an untyped `org` parameter (RpcUserOrganizationContext | None).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `def get_document_origin(org) -> str:` with an untyped `org` parameter, but this is a typing/style nit rather than a concrete defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior. Nothing in the diff indicates strict typing requirements or that this causes incorrect runtime behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch leaves `pipeline` untyped unlike sibling GitHubInstallation.dispatch (pipeline: Pipeline).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `OAuthLoginView.dispatch(self, request: Request, pipeline)` lacking a `Pipeline` type annotation, while `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` uses `pipeline: Pipeline`. However, this is a typing/style consistency nit and not a verifiable correctness or behavior defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:19 — Integration module now imports identity-provider internals (GitHubIdentityProvider, get_user_info) and hand-calls its URL/secret getters, coupling integration and identity layers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `from sentry.identity.github import GitHubIdentityProvider, get_user_info` in `integration.py` and the new `OAuthLoginView` directly instantiates `GitHubIdentityProvider()` and calls `get_oauth_client_id()`, `get_oauth_client_secret()`, `get_oauth_authorize_url()`, `get_oauth_access_token_url()`, and `get_user_info(...)`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded layering/architecture coupling between the GitHub integration pipeline and the identity-provider implementation details, but it does not by itself demonstrate a correctness/security defect in the changed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — Bare `except Exception` silently swallows token-response decode errors with no logging, hiding OAuth failures from diagnosis.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange response parsing is wrapped in `try: body = safe_urlread(req).decode(...); payload = dict(parse_qsl(body)) except Exception: payload = {}`. This does indeed swallow all decode/parse errors without logging/metrics, and then falls through to `if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)`, making OAuth failures harder to diagnose. However, the diff still handles the failure path safely (shows an error), so this is primarily an observability/debuggability issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize URL built via f-string concatenation without urlencode for redirect_uri/state; use urlencode for correctness and readability.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch the authorize redirect URL is assembled via f-string concatenation: `...?client_id=...&state=...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}`. The diff shows `redirect_uri` is built from `absolute_uri(reverse(...))` and is not URL-encoded; while the current value in tests contains only `:` and `/` and likely works, this construction is error-prone and can break if `redirect_uri` (or other params) ever contains characters like `&`, `?`, or spaces. Using `urllib.parse.urlencode` (or similar) would be more robust and readable, but the diff does not prove a current functional failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:397 — installation_id binding is split across OAuthLoginView and GitHubInstallation (bound in both), making state ownership unclear.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `installation_id` being written to pipeline state in two places: `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` binds it when present in the initial GET (so it survives the OAuth redirect), and `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` both reads from GET or `pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")` and then binds it again. This is not an outright defect (it’s consistent with preserving state across steps), but it does introduce duplicated state mutation across views that can make it harder to reason about which step “owns” the state value and when it should be set/validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:41 — Removed FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR constant in favor of hardcoded "github" literal; unrelated refactor to intent that reduces extensibility.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR = ["github"]` and replaces the membership check with `provider_id == "github"`, but this is functionally equivalent (the constant only contained a single value) and the claimed “reduced extensibility” is speculative/style-oriented rather than a concrete, diff-verifiable issue affecting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Magic pipeline-signature string and code/state setup URL are duplicated across many tests; extract a helper/constant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated hard-coded OAuth callback query parameters across multiple tests, including the same `state` value (`9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`) and `code` (`12345678901234567890`) being embedded into setup URLs in `assert_setup_flow`, `test_github_installed_on_another_org`, `test_github_user_mismatch`, and the pending-deletion tests. This duplication is diff-grounded and suggests extracting a helper/constant for maintainability, but it is not a correctness defect in the production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Test asserts on responses.calls[2] positional index, brittle coupling to stub call ordering.

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py within assert_setup_flow, the assertion was changed from `responses.calls[0]...` to `responses.calls[2]...` (line noted ~257 in the diff context). This hard-codes the expected position of the GitHub API call in the `responses` call list, which is tightly coupled to the exact sequence/number of HTTP requests (now including the new OAuth token and /user calls). Any future addition/reordering of stubbed requests would break the test without a behavioral regression, making it brittle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen token exchange is outside the try block, so network errors/timeouts/RestrictedIPAddress propagate as an unhandled 500 instead of the error page.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange call `req = safe_urlopen(...)` occurs before the `try:` block that only wraps `safe_urlread(req)`/parsing. Any exception raised by `safe_urlopen` itself (e.g., network timeout, connection error, or IP restriction) would bypass the error handling and likely result in an unhandled 500 instead of returning the integration-failed error page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is uncaught and raises (raise_for_status/JSON decode) on GitHub 401/5xx/rate limit, crashing the pipeline with a 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` which calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` directly (no `try/except` around it). The view otherwise returns a friendly `error(...)` response on invalid OAuth/token conditions, but any exception raised inside `get_user_info` (e.g., due to upstream HTTP failure/401/5xx/invalid JSON) will bubble up and produce a 500, crashing the pipeline instead of showing the intended failure page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Token exchange response status is never checked; non-200 GitHub responses are only detected indirectly via a missing access_token with no reason surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange uses `req = safe_urlopen(...)` and then parses the body via `safe_urlread(req)` into `payload`, only gating on `"access_token" not in payload` to show a generic error. There is no explicit HTTP status check or surfaced error detail in this diff. However, whether non-200 responses are actually returned (vs raising from `safe_urlopen`) is not verifiable from the diff alone, so this is a valid robustness/diagnostics concern rather than a clearly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:429 — Broad except Exception swallows read/decode failures with no logging or metrics, making OAuth failures undiagnosable.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, after calling safe_urlopen, the code wraps safe_urlread(req).decode(...) and parse_qsl(...) in `except Exception: payload = {}` with no logging/metrics. Any network/read/decode/parsing failure becomes an indistinguishable “Invalid installation request” error (`if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)`), making OAuth token exchange failures hard to diagnose. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/maintainability issue rather than a functional defect, since failures still lead to a controlled error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:438 — All OAuth failure branches (state mismatch, no access_token, no login, GitHub error payload) return a generic error with no logger/metrics call.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, all failure paths (`state` mismatch, token exchange parse failure leading to missing `access_token`, missing `login` in `get_user_info`, etc.) return `error(request, self.active_organization)` without emitting any logging or metrics (no `metrics.*` calls and no logger usage in this new code). This is verifiable from the diff and is an observability/debuggability gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for existing integrations whose metadata lacks sender, causing a 500 for reinstalls.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, when an `Integration` exists but no `OrganizationIntegration` exists, the new verification does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without guarding for missing keys. If an existing integration record’s `metadata` lacks `sender` or `login` (not enforced anywhere in this diff), this will raise `KeyError` and 500 the reinstall/rehydration flow. The diff newly introduces this unhandled access path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — Synchronous OAuth token exchange and user lookup run in the request thread with no retry and only the default safe_urlopen timeout, so a slow GitHub can hang the web worker.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, which performs a synchronous OAuth access-token exchange (`req = safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)`) and then a synchronous GitHub user lookup (`authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])`) in the request path. There is no explicit timeout passed to `safe_urlopen` and no retry/backoff logic shown around either network call. While the claim that this will "hang the web worker" depends on `safe_urlopen`/`get_user_info` defaults not visible in the diff, the architectural concern (blocking external calls on the web request thread without explicit safeguards) is directly grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — If the GitHub /user payload is not a dict (e.g. an error list or None), the `"login" in` check can raise TypeError instead of returning the error page.

adjudication.rationale: In the new OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the code does `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(...)` followed by `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info:`. This assumes `authenticated_user_info` is an iterable container (ideally a dict). The diff does not show any type/None guarding, so if `get_user_info` can ever return `None` or another non-iterable on failure, this would raise a `TypeError` instead of rendering the intended error page. However, the diff does not include `get_user_info`’s implementation, so it’s not verifiable from the PR alone that such a non-dict/non-iterable return can occur in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook not received), GitHubInstallation calls next_step without any sender/authenticated-user check, so an attacker can claim a victim's fresh installation_id and bypass the new verification.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, if `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately does `return pipeline.next_step()` (no sender/authenticated-user validation). The new verification comparing `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` only runs in the later branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` row exists. Therefore, when the webhook hasn’t created the `Integration` row yet, a caller who supplies a fresh `installation_id` can still advance the pipeline without the new authenticity check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:447 — installation_id taken from request.GET on the post-OAuth request overrides the value bound before authorization, letting the ID be swapped after the OAuth step; only the Integration-exists branch re-validates it.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, `installation_id = request.GET.get("installation_id")` is bound into pipeline state unconditionally, even on the post-OAuth callback request (i.e., when `state`/`code` are present). Then in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is taken from `request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`, so any `installation_id` query param on the callback overrides the pre-OAuth value. The only subsequent check tying the authenticated GitHub user to the installation is in the branch where an `Integration` already exists (`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` comparison). If the `Integration` does not exist (`except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()`), there is no verification preventing swapping the installation ID after OAuth, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — Authorize redirect URL built with f-string without URL-encoding client_id/state/redirect_uri (redirect_uri contains ://, /), risking malformed or parameter-injected OAuth requests; use urlencode.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch the authorize URL is constructed via an f-string: `...?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` rather than using `urlencode` for query parameters. However, the diff shows these values are internally generated (client_id/secret from provider config, `state` from `pipeline.signature`, and `redirect_uri` from `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`) and are not user-controlled here, so the claimed parameter-injection risk is not directly verifiable from the diff. Using `urlencode` would still be a robustness/best-practice improvement (e.g., if redirect_uri ever gains its own query params), but it’s not clearly a concrete defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuth state compared to pipeline.signature with != (non-constant-time) and state is a static per-pipeline signature rather than a fresh random nonce; use constant_time_compare.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the code does compare the OAuth `state` using a normal string inequality (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature:`). A constant-time comparison could be preferable for secret-like tokens. However, the finding’s additional claim that `pipeline.signature` is “static per-pipeline signature rather than a fresh random nonce” is not verifiable from this diff alone (we can’t see how `pipeline.signature` is generated), so treating this as a security-hardening concern rather than a confirmed defect is more appropriate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:398 — installation_id from the initial GET is bound into pipeline state before OAuth with no validation, and the check at 503 assumes integration.metadata["sender"] exists (KeyError -> 500 instead of a safe denial).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new denial check in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` that directly indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` (near the end of the method). If an existing `Integration` row lacks `metadata.sender` or `metadata.sender.login` (e.g., older/partially-populated records), this will raise `KeyError` and produce a 500 instead of returning the intended `error(...)` response. The first part of the finding (binding `installation_id` into pipeline state before OAuth) is accurate from `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, but the clearly verifiable defect in this diff is the unguarded metadata indexing that can crash the request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — Broad except Exception around the token exchange silently swallows errors and GitHub error responses (e.g. bad_verification_code) with no logging, hindering detection of abuse.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange/parsing block wraps `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` and `dict(parse_qsl(body))` in `except Exception: payload = {}` with no logging. This will mask parsing/IO errors and any unexpected response format, collapsing all failures into a generic `error(...)` response (`if "access_token" not in payload`). That’s a concrete, diff-grounded observability/diagnostics concern, but the flow still fails closed (no token => error page), so it’s not a directly verifiable functional/security defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:388 — test_installation_not_found now fails at the OAuth state check (different hardcoded state), so it no longer exercises the "installation could not be found" path it was written to test.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_installation_not_found`, the new request uses a hardcoded `state` value (`ddd023d8...`) that differs from the pipeline signature used elsewhere in this file (`9cae5e88...`, asserted in `assert_setup_flow`). In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, a `state` mismatch immediately returns `error(...)` before any installation lookup logic runs. The test now asserts `"Invalid installation request."` and no longer exercises the prior "installation could not be found" scenario it was named to cover (coverage/name mismatch), though it likely does not literally "fail" given the updated assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — The only negative assertion is the generic "Invalid installation request." string, which the state-mismatch, missing-token, missing-login, inactive-integration, and sender-mismatch branches all return, so the test can't tell which guard fired.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `test_github_user_mismatch`, the failure condition is asserted primarily via `assert b"Invalid installation request." in resp.content`, but that same string is returned by multiple guards introduced in this diff (e.g. state mismatch in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, missing/invalid access token or user login in the OAuth exchange, `Integration.DoesNotExist`/inactive integration, and the final sender/login mismatch check in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`). The test also checks the failed template and generic postMessage payload, which likewise don’t distinguish the specific branch. This makes the test less targeted to the intended sender-mismatch guard and could pass even if an earlier guard fired.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Hardcoded pipeline.signature values ("9cae5e88..."/"ddd023d8...") tie the tests to how signatures are generated and to fixture ordering, so they break for reasons unrelated to OAuth behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes specific `state` values in multiple tests (e.g. `assert_setup_flow` asserts the redirect query contains `state=9cae5e...` and later calls the setup endpoint with that same hardcoded state; `test_installation_not_found` uses `state=ddd023...`). Since `OAuthLoginView` compares `request.GET["state"]` to `pipeline.signature`, these tests are coupled to the exact signature value produced by the pipeline implementation, making them brittle if signature generation or pipeline initialization details change. This is a test robustness/maintainability concern, not a production behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — No dedicated test sends a forged/mismatched state and asserts the error, so the core CSRF guard is only covered by accident.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a state check in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`). A new/updated test exercises an invalid state: `test_installation_not_found` performs a callback to `self.setup_path` with `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"` (not the expected pipeline signature used elsewhere: `9cae5e...`) and asserts `"Invalid installation request."` is returned. This is a direct mismatched-state/error-path test, not merely “covered by accident.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:431 — No test covers a token-exchange response missing access_token (e.g. GitHub error=bad_verification_code) or an unparseable body.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new OAuth token-exchange logic in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` that parses the `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` response via `parse_qsl`, falls back to `payload = {}` on exceptions, and errors when `"access_token" not in payload`. The updated tests only stub a successful token response (`body=f"access_token={access_token}"`) and do not exercise the error branches where GitHub returns an error/missing `access_token` or an unparseable body, so this is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — No test covers get_user_info failing (non-200 /user), which likely raises out of dispatch as a 500 instead of rendering the error page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new OAuth step (OAuthLoginView.dispatch) that calls get_user_info(payload["access_token"]) without any exception handling; only the presence of a "login" key is checked afterward. The added tests stub a successful /user response (json={"login": "octocat"}) and cover a user-mismatch scenario via webhook metadata, but do not cover the case where the /user request fails (non-200/exception). Whether this becomes a 500 depends on get_user_info’s internal behavior (not shown in the diff), so the “likely raises as 500” part isn’t strictly verifiable, but the missing test coverage for this new failure mode is concrete and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:435 — No test covers a /user response that lacks "login".

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new logic in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` that calls `get_user_info(...)` and explicitly errors if the `/user` payload lacks a `"login"` key (`if "login" not in authenticated_user_info: return error(...)`). The added tests only stub `/user` with `{"login": "octocat"}` and cover other failure modes (e.g., state mismatch / attacker sender), but there is no test exercising the branch where `/user` responds without `login`, so the finding is accurate and points to an untested edge-case in newly added behavior rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — Only the mismatch case is tested; no test shows an existing Integration without an OrganizationIntegration succeeding when the sender login matches the authenticated user, nor covers missing metadata["sender"] (KeyError).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new authorization logic in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` that allows proceeding when an `Integration` exists but no `OrganizationIntegration` exists, gated by `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The added tests cover the mismatch case (`test_github_user_mismatch`) and other failure paths, but there is no test exercising the corresponding success path where the sender login matches and the flow continues. Additionally, the new code directly indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` without guarding for missing keys; there is no test covering missing/legacy metadata, so a potential `KeyError` edge case is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:495 — The new branch for an existing Integration that is not ACTIVE is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` for the case where an `Integration` exists but is not `ObjectStatus.ACTIVE`: it now does `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` and returns `error(...)` on `Integration.DoesNotExist` (which will occur if the integration exists but is non-ACTIVE). The added/modified tests cover OAuth flow, "installed on another org", pending deletion, installation not found (invalid request), and GitHub user mismatch, but none set up an existing integration with a non-ACTIVE status to exercise this new branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — responses.calls[2] is a brittle positional index that depends on the number and order of the OAuth HTTP calls.

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py, assert_setup_flow now asserts `auth_header = responses.calls[2].request.headers["Authorization"]`. The diff adds two new HTTP calls during the OAuth step (`POST https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` and `GET /user`), making the desired JWT-authenticated GitHub API call land at index 2 today. This is inherently brittle: any future change that adds/removes/reorders mocked HTTP requests in the flow will shift `responses.calls[...]` and break the test even if behavior is correct. This is a test robustness issue rather than a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:123 — The mocked token and /user responses are never asserted on (code/client_secret in the POST body, token in the Authorization header), so the tests would pass even if the wrong code or token were sent.

adjudication.rationale: In tests, `_stub_github()` stubs the OAuth access-token exchange (`responses.POST` to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token`) and the GitHub `/user` call, but the assertions only check the authorize redirect URL and later a JWT `Authorization` header for the *app installation access_tokens* request (`responses.calls[2]`). There is no assertion that the token exchange POST body contained the expected `code`/`client_secret` (the stub doesn’t match on body), nor that the `/user` request used the returned `access_token` in an Authorization header. This makes the new OAuthLoginView flow less strongly verified, but it’s a test coverage/robustness gap rather than a defect in the shipped logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/web/frontend/pipeline_advancer.py:41 — The FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR removal and the new OAuth redirect_uri to the setup URL have no pipeline_advancer test (e.g. an OAuth callback with state but no pipeline).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new OAuthLoginView that redirects to GitHub with `redirect_uri` pointing at `reverse("sentry-extension-setup", kwargs={"provider_id": "github"})` (i.e. the pipeline advancer endpoint), and then expects the callback to continue the pipeline by validating `state` against `pipeline.signature`. In `pipeline_advancer.py`, the GitHub special-case forward logic was also modified (removing `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR` and inlining `provider_id == "github"`). The updated integration tests exercise the OAuth redirect and callback within the existing pipeline flow, but the diff does not add a targeted test for the pipeline_advancer edge case mentioned (an OAuth callback arriving at the setup URL with `state` present but no pipeline found), which is a specific new/changed interaction between the OAuth callback and pipeline_advancer routing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:229 — No test covers a direct-from-GitHub install where installation_id arrives on the OAuth view and must survive through pipeline state into GitHubInstallation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior where `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` binds `installation_id` from `request.GET` into pipeline state (`pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", installation_id)`), and `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` now falls back to `pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")` when `installation_id` is not in `request.GET`. The updated tests (e.g. `assert_setup_flow`) still supply `installation_id` directly to the later setup request (`self.client.get(...installation_id...)`) and even assert the GitHub OAuth authorize redirect query lacks `installation_id`, so they do not exercise the path where `installation_id` is only present on the OAuth view and must persist via pipeline state into `GitHubInstallation`.
